text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Junior budget minister Ali Brahiti says the struggle to tame inflation is decisive battle to achieve economic reforms.

- Government gives politicians 72 extra hours to complete filing applications for June 5 parliamentary elections but did not extend the Monday deadline for candidate lists. Political parties must submit lists before midnight (2300 GMT) Monday and then complete legal documents necessary for the candidates' applications within three days.

- Air Algerie delays resuming flights to Paris because of technical problems at Roissy Charles de Gaulle airport and its heavy schedule to carry pilgrims to Mecca, in Saudi Arabia. The Algerian airline stopped flights to the French capital in 1995 in a row over security arrangements with the authorities.
- Politicians officially blame bureaucracy for delay in filing candidate lists but the problem lies in political parties' inability to forge consensus over who should lead constituency lists.
- Former ruling National Liberation Front excludes allies of Abdelhamid Mehri, former party head, from candidate lists to compete in the poll.

- Algiers will be the site of the parliamentary election battle between major party leaders. Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia, former prime minister Redha Malek, anti-Islamist politician Said Saadi, main legal Islamist party chief Mahfoud Nahnah and left-wing Workers Party leader Louisa Hanoune will lead their respective party flags in the capital for the June 5 elections.
